_comment: Alliances and rivalries as events: calls for help, betrayals, proposals, rivals at work, officers who leave for their own ships. scripts/bonds.gd queues the calls and betrayals; see docs/events.md.

ally_calls_for_help.title: {ally} calls for help
ally_calls_for_help.text: A fast boat brings word from {ally}: they're in a fight with a {nation_adj} ship and need you. You're bound to answer, and it will cost you.

choices.result: You come up under full sail, guns run out.
Not what they asked for, but something.
They'll remember who didn't come.

ally_betrays.title: Treachery
ally_betrays.text: Word reaches you that {ally} has been talking to the {nation_adj} authorities about your course, your haunts and your hold. Your ally has decided you're worth more sold than kept.

choices.result: You slip away before the trap closes. {ally} is your enemy now.
choices.fail_result: Too late: a warship is already on your course.

choices.result: {ally} backs down and swears it was a misunderstanding. Now they owe you.
choices.fail_result: {ally} laughs, and your secrets are already sold.

captain_proposes.title: A proposal from {captain}
captain_proposes.text: {captain} sends a bottle of good brandy and a note: two captains who keep out of each other's way do better than two who don't.

choices.result: Neither of you will fire on the other.
No hard feelings. Probably.

rival_taunt.title: {rival}'s men
rival_taunt.text: In a {port} tavern, some of {rival}'s crew are drinking to your hanging. One of them spits at your feet.

choices.result: They carry their man out. Your crew will tell the story for weeks.
choices.fail_result: It ends with you bleeding on the floor and them laughing.

choices.text: Buy the room a round and drink to {rival}'s ruin
choices.result: The whole tavern drinks with you. Word will reach {rival}.
Your crew wanted more from you.

rival_sabotage.title: {rival} has friends ashore
rival_sabotage.text: The harbour master of {port} has suddenly found faults with your papers. {rival}'s money got here before you did.

choices.result: Money talks louder than grudges, today.
The faults disappear.
choices.fail_result: Two days kicking your heels while they inspect every barrel.

choices.result: Cheaper than a fight.

rival_offers_peace.title: A message from {rival}
rival_offers_peace.text: {rival} sends word: there are bigger sharks in these waters than either of you. Perhaps it's time to bury the hatchet.

choices.result: The feud is over. For now.
The crew cheer. The feud goes on.

officer_wants_own_ship.title: A ship of their own
officer_wants_own_ship.text: {officer} has served you well, and wants what every good officer wants: a command of their own. They mean to go, with or without your blessing.

choices.text: Go with my blessing, and a loan for a sloop
choices.result: {officer} sails as your friend, and owes you.
You part on good terms.
One more voyage, {officer} agrees.
choices.fail_result: {officer} goes anyway, angry, and talks about you in every tavern.

deserter_knows_a_ship.title: A deserter's tale
deserter_knows_a_ship.text: A sailor who jumped ship from {captain}'s crew is drinking alone in {port}. For the price of a few more drinks, the sailor would gladly tell where that ship is rotten, undermanned or slow.

choices.text: Buy the drinks and listen (40 gold)
choices.result: You leave with a page of notes on every weakness of {captain}'s ship.
Not your concern.

rival_spy.title: Eyes on {rival}
rival_spy.text: A boatman in {port} offers to row out at night and look over {rival}'s ship at anchor: the rig, the timbers, how many hands stand watch.

choices.result: The boatman comes back with everything. Next time you meet {rival}, you'll know where to strike.
choices.fail_result: The boatman is caught and talks. {rival} knows you're watching.

choices.result: You'll take {rival} as you find them.
